premise: At 58, I cashed out $132,000 of my 30-year mail-carrier pension to co-found a vintage watch-and-clock restoration studio with my former daughter-in-law, notarizing a 50% stake and free watch batteries for my widows' group, but after a luxury auction house offered $710,000 for the restored Patek Philippe parts inventory and client list she forged a dissolution, sold the assets, and mailed me a $4,300 'mainspring' check; I recovered our original agreement from a hollowed wooden watch case, voided the sale, and now run 'Crown of Deceit Horology,' where she polishes crystals in a smock that says 'Wound Me Out' and every repair ticket prints her fraud docket.
